take_homes: Ask three questions before connecting an agent to anything: what may it read, what may it change, what must go back to a human. Closing a door is the cheapest fix and it costs a feature.
When the check says 'I can't tell', take the evidence to the owner (DPO, legal, IT) with one narrow question.
You can save a company-specific check as a skill and hand it to someone else. It sits on top of normal controls and doesn't replace them.

monday.move: Write the three questions (read, change, back to a human) for my weekly people-metrics summary idea. Then email our DPO the 'can't tell' question about employee data in an AI tool before I build anything.
monday.who: Me and our DPO, then one HR partner
monday.when: Monday morning, ahead of the leadership meeting
monday.stop_condition: If the DPO says employee data can't go in this tool, I stop and take it to the works council first.
monday.blocker: The works council and DPO have not been asked about employee data yet.

misconception.why: The module is about what an agent can reach and who signs off, and it never talks about which roles go. That moved my attention from headcount to access and checks. It never addressed headcount directly, so I still expect it to come up in the leadership meeting.

one_line: Useful if you want a way to think about what an agent may touch, but there are nine 'rapidly evolving area' paragraphs in the way, and the people side was only touched when I raised it myself.
